short: HMM phone recognizer (M06) standard; recognition-then-unit-selection output (M08) departs from frame-wise mapping, incl. the group's 2007 one, but is tested only on oracle phones.
position: The paper [@hueber2010development] changes two components. Its visual phone recognizer (M06) is standard, a context-independent HMM-GMM like 10 of the 12 prior articulatory-signal recognizers (Appendix), and below the context-dependent multi-stream decoder of the group's [concurrent] study on a larger set of the same corpus [@hueber2009visuo]. Its output route (M08), phone recognition then diphone unit selection, departs from the frame-wise mapping of all three prior output studies, including the group's 2007 neural mapping [@hueber2007eigentongue; @kaburagi1998determination; @engwall2005articulatory], but is standard by rule: that 2007 mapping is not compared on the same data or measure, and synthesis is tested only on oracle phones (§5.3). The "reasonable approach" claim (§5.3) rests on that test; the authors state that about 60% phone accuracy is not enough for intelligible synthesis (§6), that output from recognized phones is not evaluated (§5.3), and that all data are uttered speech (Introduction).
